key_insight: Pretraining on a large CFD dataset can significantly reduce data needs when transferring neural PDE surrogates to a new geometry, but the benefit depends on the type of distribution shift. The paper shows that matching the freestream range is not enough—changes in underlying modeled physics can alter how much pretraining helps.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to predict and improve pretraining gains for neural PDE surrogates when moving from one airflow/airfoil distribution to another, especially when geometry changes and the target physics may differ.
method: Pretrain a neural PDE surrogate on 254,909 RANS simulations from one airfoil family.
Fine-tune the pretrained model on a different airfoil family under two target settings: same Spalart-Allmaras (SA) turbulence modeling and SA plus e^N transition modeling.
Compare performance at limited data budgets to isolate how different components of distribution shift affect transfer benefits.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides evidence that transfer learning for scientific surrogates is sensitive to both geometry and physics mismatch. It helps guide when pretraining is likely to reduce CFD data requirements and when domain shifts may weaken its advantage.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing pretraining on source airfoils and fine-tuning on target airfoils
Side-by-side comparison of the two target settings: SA vs SA + e^N transition
Bar chart or line plot of error versus number of target samples, highlighting gains from pretraining
Icon-based summary of distribution shift components: geometry, freestream conditions, and modeled physics
paper_title: How Does Distribution Shift Shape Pretraining Gains in Neural PDE Surrogates?
paper_authors: Pochinapeddi Sai Bhargav, Nithin Somasekharan, Rohit Sunil Kanchi, Sicheng He, Shaowu Pan
